explain.say: A data centre is a building packed with thousands of computers called servers, and almost all the electricity they use ends up as heat. Without cooling, the chips would overheat within minutes.

faq.q: Why do servers get so hot?
faq.a: Chips use electricity to switch billions of transistors, and nearly all of that energy turns into heat. A rack of servers can give off as much heat as several electric heaters running at full power.
asks: Where does a computer's heat come from?

faq.a: A cold aisle is the corridor in front of the server racks, where cool air is delivered. Servers all face it, pulling cool air in at the front and blowing warm air out at the back.
The aisle behind the racks, where hot air comes out, is closed off with doors and a roof so the hot air cannot mix back into the cold aisle. This makes cooling much more efficient.
asks: Why are hot and cold air kept apart in a data centre?

faq.q: How does a data centre get rid of the heat?
faq.a: Air handlers move the heat into chilled water, and chillers, cooling towers or dry coolers on the roof release it to the outside air. In cool climates, outside air can do most of the work for free.
asks: How do chillers work in a data centre?

faq.q: Can data centre heat be reused?
faq.a: Yes. Some data centres, for example in Nordic countries, pipe their warm water into district heating networks that heat homes and offices nearby.

facts: Data centres used roughly 1 to 1.5 percent of the world's electricity in 2022, according to International Energy Agency estimates.
Power usage effectiveness (PUE) compares a data centre's total power with the power used by its computers; a PUE of 1.0 would mean zero cooling overhead.

quiz.say: Why is the hot aisle behind the server racks walled off?
quiz.show: The hot aisle is closed off to…

options.show: Keep hot and cold air from mixing
options.say: Keep hot and cold air from mixing

quiz.why: Keeping warm exhaust air away from the cold supply air means the servers always breathe cool air, and cooling uses less energy.

wrong.1: Walls do not change server speed directly; they make cooling efficient.
wrong.2: The reason is airflow, not looks.
